title: Top-Down RPG Demo [Godot + Claude + Blender]
author: Antique_Angle_8076
selftext:
Initially started out as a capability test for Claude Opus 5.5, which turned out to be quite good so I wanted to stress test it. I ended up with a fully functional demo of a sandbox open world with **NPC routines, dynamic weather, day-night cycles, Wildlife and enemy simulations.**

At some point the system became quite complex to control with just prompts so I vibe-coded an interface for Godot and Claude to control Dialog Interactions, Direct Quests, Manage assets and keep track of game systems.

AMA

comments.author: SeventhMind7
comments.body: wow you're giving me hope for the visual side of my godot project. Can you share a little about how you got the assets/animation to look so good?

replies.author: Antique_Angle_8076
replies.body:
Yes Godot is actually very capable !  
Since its a light weight engine it doesn't have a lot of tools / Shader packed in like Unreal or Unity  
The beauty of Agent Assistant Development is that you can ask the agent to build those tools and systems for you.

So that's what I did I vibe coded the system one by one then asked the agent to assemble them  
The world is procedurally generated meaning its built in code and deployed in runtime similar to how No Man's Sky works

I built systems to control the procedural generations instead of modeling the world, If you look towards the end of the video you'll find the interface which is used to control the world.

replies.author: Unfixab1e
replies.body:
wow good job on the demo! I started with a small map/ui editor for development of my tactical rpg as well but you went much further and it immediately gave me dozens of new ideas!

you mentioned procedural generations, do you mean the assets are also generated in code or did you use meshy/tripo to generate/rig them and then import them using your tooling?

replies.author: Antique_Angle_8076
replies.body:
I’m treating the assets as placeholders for now.  
They were made by Claude using Blender MCP  
Characters assets are meshy (since I found out Opus 5.5 is not that good at character design )  
Rigging for characters was done in meshy itself.  
Claude can also do rigging and animation using blender MCP, but it’s a hit or miss.

replies.author: Unfixab1e
replies.body: Ah I see, thanks for the info - art style already looks great for them being placeholders. I also ran into issues with animation myself,  soI forked [https://github.com/Mesh2Motion/mesh2motion-app](https://github.com/Mesh2Motion/mesh2motion-app) and integrated it into a rigging/animation editor which worked quite well. Claude had an easier time rigging models than with blender mcp but I still had to manually fix stuff sometimes. it also includes many license free animations which was a plus.
